Ranked last here purely because it is the only step on this list that needs a file from outside the warehouse -- but it has by far the widest blast radius, since the same polygons turn Mass, KDE, hotspot analysis, Moran's I and Voronoi from dots-and-surfaces into filled areas in one go.

opportunity_findings.detail: Flow maps is scored PARTIAL on the blocker 'nothing in the warehouse can place a ZIP on a map,' but the pieces to place a ZIP are both in LIBRARY_MARTS.CORE and were checked column by column: XWALK_ZCTA_COUNTY (46,960 rows) carries ZCTA5, COUNTY_FIPS and STATE_FIPS, and DIM_COUNTY (3,222 rows) carries POP_CENTER_LAT and POP_CENTER_LON as FLOAT. ZIP to county to centroid is a two-hop join with no ingest. The scoring is right that no ZIP-level centroid exists, but wrong that ZIP flows therefore cannot be drawn -- they can be drawn at county resolution today. On top of that, FEMA's origin end needs no crosswalk at all: HOUSING__FED_FEMA_IA_HOUSING_REGISTRATIONS carries CENSUS_GEOID, which joins directly to DIM_TRACT.TRACT_GEOID and its centroid. This changes the opportunity picture because it moves flow maps from 'needs a data source we do not have' to 'needs one dbt model over two tables we do have.'

No scoring row mentions LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__XC_EPA_CORPORATE_CROSSWALK, and it is the single most consequential omission in the whole set. Verified: 5,300,149 rows -- exactly one per row of ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_FRS_FACILITIES -- with EPA_REGISTRY_ID, FACILITY_NAME, MATCHED_LEI, MATCHED_LEGAL_NAME, MATCH_METHOD, MATCH_CONFIDENCE (NUMBER), ULTIMATE_PARENT_LEI, PARENT_LEGAL_NAME, PARENT_CIK, PARENT_UEI, REVIEW_FLAG (BOOLEAN). This is a pre-built bridge from GLEIF's LEI namespace onto 5.3M geocoded, FIPS-stamped facilities, and onward to the SEC family through PARENT_CIK (CIK appears in 20+ FINANCE and ECONOMICS mart tables) and to federal money through PARENT_UEI (RECIPIENT_UEI / RECIPIENT_PARENT_UEI on USASpending contracts 20,000,000 and assistance 19,902,879). Three separate scoring rows -- Circulation, Ripples and connectome mapping -- describe the corporate lane as sealed or as reaching only 'nine other mart tables,' and all three are working from an incomplete picture. Caveat that must travel with this: MATCH_METHOD/MATCH_CONFIDENCE/REVIEW_FLAG mark it as a fuzzy name match, and the non-null fill rate of MATCHED_LEI is unverified from metadata.

The connectome row calls the islands untouchable and BRIDGE_ENTITIES empty, but LIBRARY_MARTS.FINDINGS holds 13 pre-built cross-domain views that already traverse islands, and one of them proves the corporate chain works end to end: FEDERAL_CONTRACTOR_EPA_VIOLATOR carries PARENT_UEI, COMPANY_NAME, VIOLATING_FACILITIES, ANY_SNC, TOTAL_EPA_PENALTIES, TOTAL_FORMAL_ACTIONS, FEDERAL_DOLLARS_OBLIGATED, N_AWARDS, N_AGENCIES and MATCH_CONFIDENCE on one row. Its siblings do the same for other lanes -- EXCLUDED_PROVIDER_PAID_AFTER_EXCLUSION_IN_SHORTAGE, OPIOID_PRESCRIBER_PAID_HIGH_RX, PAC_FUNDS_BOTH_SIDES, REVOKED_BUT_DEDUCTIBLE, HOSPITAL_CLOSURE_RISK. These are views, so ALL_TABLES.csv reports no row count for them and I cannot say how many rows each returns -- but their existence contradicts the flat claim that cross-island joins are not running. Note the honest counterweight: TOTAL_EPA_PENALTIES on that view is drawing from the EPA penalty column the 2026-07-27 sweep flagged for stamping one settlement onto hundreds of facilities.

The Ripples row states GLEIF RELATIONSHIPS 'carries five period start/end pairs but all ten are TEXT.' That is true and I confirmed it, but the row omits that the same table already carries three real DATE columns -- REGISTRATION_INITIALREGISTRATIONDATE, REGISTRATION_LASTUPDATEDATE and REGISTRATION_NEXTRENEWALDATE -- and reports/time_index/clock_index.csv rates all three at HIGH confidence, noting they come from a guarded to_date(try_to_timestamp_tz(...)) parse already applied inside that dbt model. So a dated ownership animation runs today off the registration clock, and the outstanding cast is a copy-paste of a cast sitting in the same file rather than new work. The clock index also already ruled the period columns as span_start/span_end at day grain and wrote down the trap in writing: the five slots are a flattened repeating group, so you must filter RELATIONSHIP_PERIOD_1_PERIODTYPE = 'RELATIONSHIP_PERIOD' first.

LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__MEMBER_CROSSWALK (12,794 rows) appears in no scoring row, and it is the identifier Rosetta stone for a domain prior sessions recorded as having zero verified cross-family joins. Verified columns: MEMBER_KEY, BIOGUIDE, ICPSR, GOVTRACK, OPENSECRETS, VOTESMART, LIS, THOMAS, CSPAN, WIKIDATA, BALLOTPEDIA, WIKIPEDIA, HOUSE_HISTORY, MAPLIGHT, GOOGLE_ENTITY_ID, FEC_IDS (VARIANT), plus name, party, state and term fields. The downstream tables that should be consuming it are starved: POLITICS__MEMBER_FEC_ID holds 1,715 rows and MEMBER_INDIV_DONATIONS / MEMBER_MONEY_RAISED / MEMBER_PAC_MONEY / MEMBER_VOTING_RECORD hold 1,057 / 1,050 / 1,258 / 1,105 against a 12,794-member spine. Flattening the FEC_IDS array is a hours-long job that could scale the money-to-votes graph roughly tenfold, wiring FEC_INDIV_CONTRIBUTIONS (84,172,112) to VOTEVIEW_VOTES (945,523) and BILL_COSPONSORS (367,735).

Two scoring rows contradict each other on whether the warehouse holds any polygon. 'Sample or tier by zoom' says exactly two of 162,750 columns are real GEOGRAPHY and there is no boundary shape anywhere; 'Spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I)' says 'One absolute claim from the prior read is also wrong: a polygon layer does exist -- LIBRARY_MARTS.HOUSING.HOUSING__FED_MAPPING_INEQUALITY carries a GEOMETRY column.' Measured from ALL_COLUMNS.csv: that column is named GEOMETRY but its dtype is TEXT, and a dtype sweep of the full column census returns exactly two GEOGRAPHY columns (both MARITIME__FED_NOAA_AIS.POSITION_GEOGRAPHY, once in MARITIME and once in TIMELINE) and zero GEOMETRY-typed columns in the entire warehouse. Whether that TEXT column holds real WKT or GeoJSON cannot be determined from metadata -- call it unverified. The zoom row is right; the Moran's row overstates. This matters because the polygon gap is the one cross-cutting blocker whose fix lights up five techniques at once, and a reader who believes a polygon layer already exists will not go get one.

The absence of any national boundary polygon is the single widest constraint in the set, and it is confirmed twice over: zero GEOMETRY-typed columns and two GEOGRAPHY columns across 162,750, and a name sweep of ALL_TABLES.csv for tiger/boundary/shapefile/gazetteer/cartographic/zcta/polygon returning only LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_SUPERFUND_SITE_BOUNDARIES (2,114 rows) and LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_BIA_TRIBAL_GEO (100 rows). Every geometry-named column outside those is TEXT, and the bulk of them are city ArcGIS portal crawls in LIBRARY_STAGING.DBT_CROGERS (Harris County, Atlanta, Fort Worth, Columbus). This one gap caps 'Sample or tier by zoom' at PARTIAL and quietly degrades the rendered output of Mass, KDE, hotspot analysis, Moran's I and Voronoi from filled areas to dots and surfaces, even though all five are correctly scored READY on the statistics. One TIGER ingest keyed on the FIPS codes DIM_STATE, DIM_COUNTY and DIM_TRACT already carry lifts all of them together.

The shape of nearly every cheap unlock on this list is the same: the value is present but stored as text. 91.6% of all columns are TEXT (149,003 of 162,750) against 7,558 NUMBER, 2,150 DATE and 2,064 FLOAT. 805 tables have a latitude-named column and only 122 store it as a number; 4,977 money columns exist and 3,478 are TEXT; 12,562 date-ish columns exist and 9,385 are TEXT. The pattern the verified-facts file records is that the mart layer is where casts happened and the raw landing copies are still text -- so the generic form of a small-effort unlock in this warehouse is 'add a guarded cast to an existing dbt model,' which is exactly what the GLEIF period-date step is. Anyone ranking opportunities should expect the cheapest wins to be casts, and the expensive ones to be ingests and spine rebuilds.

LIBRARY_MARTS.HOUSING.HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA_ARID2017_LEI_XREF (5,399 rows, columns ARID_2017, RESPONDENT_NAME, LEI_2018, LEI_2019, LEI_2020) is an unused bridge that could pull the warehouse's largest tract-level table into the corporate ownership graph. HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA_HISTORIC holds 19,136,434 loan records carrying RESPONDENT_ID and AGENCY_CODE plus STATE_CODE, COUNTY_CODE and CENSUS_TRACT_NUMBER; the xref maps the pre-2018 respondent identifier to the LEI used from 2018 on, and LEI reaches GLEIF's 3,382,301 entities and 484,142 ownership edges. That would put lender ownership on 19.1M mortgage decisions at census-tract grain -- the redlining lane. Two honest caveats: whether ARID_2017 is simply AGENCY_CODE concatenated with RESPONDENT_ID is an assumption I could not verify from metadata, and HMDA_HISTORIC has no DATE column at all -- its only clock is AS_OF_YEAR stored as TEXT, so the joined result is year-grain at best.

The contact-tracing row treats ICE detention as a single sealed table, but LIBRARY_MARTS.IMMIGRATION.IMMIGRATION__FED_ICE_DETENTION_FACILITY_CODES (1,490 rows) carries DETENTION_FACILITY_CODE, DETENTION_FACILITY_NAME, ADDRESS, CITY, COUNTY, STATE, ZIP and LATITUDE/LONGITUDE as NUMBER -- and IMMIGRATION__FED_ICE_DETENTION_STINTS (2,571,975 rows) carries the matching DETENTION_FACILITY_CODE. That is a one-hop join putting 2.57M person-level detention stints, each with real TIMESTAMP_NTZ book-in and book-out columns, onto a map with a county key and a distance-band neighbour rule. It makes the detention data eligible for hotspot analysis, KDE and flow maps, not just contact tracing, and no scoring row claims it.

The flow-maps row states that both USASpending county FIPS columns were 'pushed through try_to_number in the Aug-10 review, along with ACTION_DATE, so the claim that it joins straight to DIM_COUNTY centroids with no name matching is false as written.' Two things soften that. The stored dtype of PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_COUNTY_FIPS_CODE and PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_COUNTY_FIPS_CODE in the mart is TEXT, not NUMBER -- so whatever the model SQL does mid-stream, the landed values are strings and may still carry their leading zeros. I cannot settle it from metadata and did not run SQL, so the honest reading is 'suspect, check the values,' not 'confirmed broken.' The distinction matters: if those two columns survived intact, the county-to-county flow lane over 19,902,879 assistance rows is READY today with no repair at all.

The Circulation row's closing note says GLEIF is 'the only one that can [cross a source boundary]' and grounds that in LEI appearing in nine other mart tables. I counted the LEI-carrying mart tables and get twelve column hits across nine distinct non-backup tables -- ECONOMICS__INTL_GLEIF, ECONOMICS__INTL_GLEIF_REPEX, ENVIRONMENT__XC_EPA_CORPORATE_CROSSWALK (MATCHED_LEI and ULTIMATE_PARENT_LEI), FINANCE__FED_FDIC_BANK_DATA, FINANCE__INTL_ISO_MIC_REGISTRY, HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA, HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA_DC_ONLY, HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA_LAR and HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA_ARID2017_LEI_XREF -- so the count is roughly right but the weighting is badly off. Three of the nine are HMDA stubs at 28,301 / 28,301 / 17,474 rows. The one that carries almost all the mass is the EPA crosswalk at 5,300,149, and it is also the only one that hands LEI a further hop to CIK and UEI. Reading 'nine tables' as nine comparable destinations overstates the breadth and badly understates the depth.
